match.reason: The new point covers what employers and employees expect of each other, but the closest bank point explains the legal instruments (contracts, awards, agreements, NES) that set pay and conditions, and the other points cover separation, inflation and quality, so none teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Employer and employee expectations
card: An expectation is what each side hopes and assumes the other will do in a working relationship. Employers and employees each have their own.
expects a signed employment contract, loyalty to the business, and fair notice when an employee plans to leave.
expects fair pay and conditions, job security, and a work-life balance, which means time for life outside work.
Expectations can clash. A business that wants staff to be flexible may meet an employee who wants set hours.
draft.remember: Each side expects something from the other: employers want commitment, employees want fairness and security.

a.q: Which of these is an employer's expectation of an employee?
opts: Giving fair notice before leaving the job
Receiving fair pay for the work done
Having time for life outside of work
Having a secure job with ongoing hours
a.why: Employers expect fair notice so they can plan and find a replacement. The other three are what employees expect from the employer, so they are not employer expectations.
a.clue: Which one is something the employer wants from staff?

b.q: Jas works at a bakery in Ballarat. She is often asked to stay late with no warning, and she has told her manager she has little time for her family. Which employee expectation is she mainly saying is not being met?
opts: Work-life balance
Job security
Fair notice
Loyalty to the business
b.why: Late shifts with no warning leave Jas with little time for family, so her work-life balance is the issue. Job security is about keeping the job, and she has not said her job is at risk.
b.clue: Look at what she says she has little time for.

a.best: Giving fair notice before leaving the job

problems.detail: The remember line sums the sides up as 'employers want commitment, employees want fairness and security'. This is a neater split than the card gives, and it drops work-life balance, which the card lists as an employee expectation and question b tests.

The stem says Jas is asked to stay late 'with no warning', which makes the distractor 'Fair notice' tempting as a lack-of-notice problem. The card defines fair notice only as an employer expectation about an employee leaving, so students may be confused.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer. The remember line oversimplifies the two sides and leaves out work-life balance. In question b, 'with no warning' could pull students towards the 'Fair notice' distractor.
